cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest living among the exiles by the River Kebar (Ezekiel 1:1-3). Far away, the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem (Ezekiel 24:2). Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel.
God calls him son of man, and then comes news I wouldn't wish on anybody. He's about to take away the desire of Ezekiel's eyes with a fatal blow.

cards.question: When God takes away the desire of Ezekiel's eyes, Ezekiel is allowed to weep and let his tears flow.

cards.text: God says to groan quietly and not mourn for the dead. Friend, I've heard some hard words in my time, but that one stops me cold.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel not to dress like a mourner. What does God tell him to wear instead?
God tells Ezekiel not to cover his lips, but says he may still eat the bread of mourners.
Ezekiel speaks to the people in the morning, and in the ___ his ___ dies.

cards.text: The next morning, Ezekiel does just as he was commanded. I bet every head in the crowd turns, and then the people ask him something.

cards.question: Ezekiel's wife has died, but he isn't mourning, and his turban and sandals are on. What do the people ask him?

answers.text: What his actions mean for them
Why God took his wife away
Why he isn't angry at God

cards.text: Ezekiel answers with the word of the LORD for the house of Israel. And here's the turn, friend: he lost the desire of his eyes, and God says Israel is about to lose the desire of theirs.

cards.question: God says He is about to desecrate the desire of Israel's eyes, the pride of their power. What is it?
God also says the sons and daughters the people left behind will fall by the sword.

cards.text: Then Ezekiel tells them they'll do just as he has done: no covering their lips, and no bread of mourners. The man is a walking preview.

cards.question: Ezekiel says that on that day, the people will take off their turbans and sandals.
Ezekiel says the people won't mourn or weep on that day. Instead, they will waste away because of their ___.
God says Ezekiel will be a sign for the people, and they'll do everything he has done. When all this happens, what does God say they will know?

answers.text: That He is the Lord GOD
That Ezekiel is a true priest

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel about the day He takes away their stronghold, their pride and joy, and their sons and daughters. On that day, a ___ will come and tell Ezekiel the news.

cards.text: Back when God first called Ezekiel, He said He'd make Ezekiel's tongue stick to the roof of his mouth so he'd be mute (Ezekiel 3:26). Ezekiel speaks when God opens his mouth to give the people a message (Ezekiel 3:27).

cards.question: On the day the fugitive brings the news, something changes for Ezekiel himself. What is it?

answers.text: He will speak and no longer be mute
He will be set free from his exile
He will see Jerusalem with his eyes

cards.text: That's a BIG day for a man whose mouth God has to open. So Ezekiel will be a sign to them, and they will know that He is the LORD.

findings.problem: The question's setup says God tells Ezekiel not to dress like a mourner and asks what he wears instead. Both wrong answers, 'Sackcloth and no sandals' and 'A torn robe and ashes', are mourning clothes, so the setup rules them out and leaves only the right answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card tells only Ezekiel 3:26-27 and cites it. It tells nothing from Ezekiel 24:15-27 and doesn't move the baker through the passage. The background about Ezekiel being mute should ride along on a card that also tells part of the passage, like the setup for card 19.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The question says 'on that day' without saying which day. That day was set up on earlier cards the baker can no longer see, which is God desecrating His sanctuary (24:21). Verse 23 itself has no 'on that day'. Card 15 uses the same pointer.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
